name: Cybersecurity
description: Thinking like an attacker and a defender: threat modelling, network, web and system security, and security operations.

nodes.name: CIA & principles
nodes.desc: Confidentiality, integrity and availability, least privilege and defence in depth.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the CIA triad, least privilege and defence in depth when reasoning about the security of a system.

nodes.name: Threat modelling
nodes.desc: Assets, attackers and attack surfaces, and STRIDE.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify assets, attackers and attack surfaces and enumerate threats systematically with STRIDE.

nodes.name: Authentication
nodes.desc: Passwords, MFA, sessions and authorisation models.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design authentication with passwords, MFA and sessions and choose an authorisation model for access control.

nodes.name: Network attacks
nodes.desc: Sniffing, spoofing, MITM, DoS and scanning.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain sniffing, spoofing, man-in-the-middle, denial of service and scanning attacks on networks.

nodes.name: Firewalls & IDS
nodes.desc: Packet filtering, segmentation and intrusion detection.
nodes.summary: You will be able to defend networks with packet filtering, segmentation and intrusion detection systems.

nodes.name: TLS & VPNs
nodes.desc: Secure channels with TLS and VPNs and certificate validation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to secure communication channels with TLS and VPNs and validate certificates correctly.

nodes.name: Wireless security
nodes.desc: Wi-Fi protocols, their attacks and securing wireless networks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare Wi-Fi security protocols, describe their attacks and secure wireless networks.

nodes.name: OWASP Top 10
nodes.desc: The most common web application vulnerabilities.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe the OWASP Top 10 web application vulnerabilities and how each is typically exploited and prevented.

nodes.name: Injection
nodes.desc: SQL, command and template injection and parameterised queries.
nodes.summary: You will be able to exploit and prevent SQL, command and template injection, primarily through parameterised queries and safe APIs.

nodes.name: XSS & CSRF
nodes.desc: Cross-site scripting, request forgery and browser defences.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain cross-site scripting and cross-site request forgery and apply browser defences against them.

nodes.name: Session security
nodes.desc: Cookies, tokens, session fixation and secure session handling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to handle sessions securely with properly configured cookies and tokens and prevent session fixation and hijacking.

nodes.name: Buffer overflows
nodes.desc: Stack and heap overflows, exploitation basics and mitigations like ASLR.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain stack and heap buffer overflows, how they are exploited and mitigations such as ASLR and stack canaries.

nodes.name: Privilege escalation
nodes.desc: Misconfigurations and vulnerabilities that turn a user into root.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify misconfigurations and vulnerabilities that let a normal user gain root or administrator privileges.

nodes.name: Malware
nodes.desc: Viruses, worms, ransomware and how they spread and persist.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify viruses, worms, trojans and ransomware and explain how malware spreads and persists.

nodes.name: Penetration testing
nodes.desc: Reconnaissance, exploitation and reporting in an authorised test.
nodes.summary: You will be able to plan and carry out an authorised penetration test from reconnaissance to exploitation and reporting.

nodes.name: Incident response
nodes.summary: You will be able to respond to a security incident through detection, containment, forensics and recovery.

nodes.name: Secure development
nodes.desc: Security reviews, dependency scanning and secure coding practices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build security into software development with reviews, dependency scanning and secure coding practices.

nodes.name: CTF challenges project
nodes.desc: Solve a set of capture-the-flag challenges across web, crypto and binary categories.
nodes.summary: You will solve a set of capture-the-flag challenges across web, cryptography and binary exploitation categories.

nodes.name: Hack & fix lab project
nodes.desc: Attack a deliberately vulnerable app in a lab, then patch every finding.
nodes.summary: You will attack a deliberately vulnerable application in a lab environment and then patch every vulnerability you find.
